questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It had to be an english speaking country, with a similar culture to ours that could provide academic and life quality.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say it was easy. The university would send emails with information and upon arrival there was people available to ask questions. They also have a student service (STOP 1) which was great for all sorts of questions (also not uni-related even)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They were good at answering all sorts of questions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was hard at first, but then another student told me to search in a Facebook group called Fairy Floss Real Estate, it is a good place to find share-houses.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would say it is a great opportunity if you want to with Aussies, since the colleges are mostly for international people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You would have to find which subjects you want to do in an online booklet that they have. I would say it is okay, however, these subjects are not always available for different reasons. The registration process itself was not so different to the one we have in KU, you have to log in into a similar site like KUNet and register the subjects you want, the order you want them and which schedule (they have to accept the subjects first but then you choose)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: STOP1 is a place where you can always go, and they will answer your questions and even help you throughout the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful. There was one subject that was already full, so I had to change it. It is always good to have second options.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read carefully the instructions, and if you have any doubt contact stop1 they will help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses is high, however the biggest difference is the workload (much higher in Melbourne)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say the style is somehow similar in most of the subjects, there is the theory part (lectures, which in my case were recordings) and then the practical part (workshops, tutorials, lab...). However, my online subject was based on podcasts, multiple choice tests and a collage.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cell Signalling and Neurochemistry
Contemporary Art and Biomedicine (online)
Protein Structure and Function
Techniques in Molecular Science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you want to have a hands-on and very practical subject with lots of lab, I recommend Techniques in Molecular Science. I wouldn't recommend having Cell Signalling and Neurochemistry and Protein Structure and Function at the same time, both are great subjects, however, both have lots of workload and almost weekly assignments (that are quite heavy).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Buying things for my lab subject (I forgot to bring my lab-coat) and my artistic subject.
Getting a diving certificate

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Sushi was very cheap. Eating out in general is very affordable compared to Denmark. 
However, fruit and vegetables if they are not on season, they are a bit more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are many club opportunities, both social and sports.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of language clubs, team sports, and other sports such as surf, diving, mountaineering...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you want to learn how to dive, I recommend joining the diving club, they offer a course where you can learn and then take on dives with the club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as you can. Near Melbourne you can go to Phillip Island, Great Ocean Road, Mornington Peninsula, lots of hikes... It is also very easy and quite cheap to travel to Tasmania from Melbourne, which I recommend. You can also find very good deals for domestic flights around Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Their culture is very open and quite similar to European culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any challenge culturally.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open and helpful they are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Join the clubs
2. Travel as much as possible
3. Be prepared mentally that the workload might be heavier than in KU

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
1. Use STOP1 whenever you have a doubt or problem (even not uni related)
2. The university has a doctor's office (in a building outside of the campus), and it is for free if you have Bupa insurance (it is the one uni melb recommends)
3. Melbourne university offers free frozen meals once a week and free vegetables and fruits once per month approx. You have to register for it, it is called Food relief (
https://students.unimelb.edu.au/student-support/health-and-wellbeing/food-relief
)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The whole experience was rewarding. Academically it was very challenging, however rewarding. All the trip opportunities was amazing, and I really enjoyed the university clubs and social life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The workload and the fact that I used more time doing uni work than expected.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
